text:
The Eagles opened the practice window Wednesday for three-time Pro Bowl left guard Landon Dickerson, who hasn’t played since a disastrous opening-day performance against Washington.

Dickerson was placed on Injured Reserve with a bone bruise in his right knee a day after the season opener, in which he admitted he was a “complete liability” because the injury hampered him so much. He said he suffered the injury during training camp and thought it would heal on its own.

“You guys know Landon well, he works hard, he's determined to get back, and I think he's done a nice job taking care of his body to get himself back,” Sirianni said Wednesday before the news was made official. “Landon's a hell of a player and he's been a hell of a player for us.”

Once placed on Injured Reserve, players must miss at least four games before becoming eligible to return. With his practice window, Dickerson is able to practice with the team while remaining on IR until he’s officially activated.

With Dickerson unavailable, the Eagles’ initially moved Cam Jurgens from center to left guard and inserted 2nd-year pro Drew Kendall at center. They ultimately traded Jurgens to the Ravens, and with Kendall out Sunday with a knee injury, they wound up with two undrafted players making their first career start on the o-line, Willie Lampkin at left guard and Jake Majors at center.

Left tackle Jordan Mailata and right guard Tyler Steen have started all five games, but the Eagles have used three left guards (Dickerson, Jurgens, Lampkin), three centers (Jurgens, Kendall, Majors) and two right tackles (Lane Johnson, Markel Bell). So they’ve had nine different o-line starters and four different offensive lines through Week 5.

The Packers are the only team that’s used more starting offensive linemen. They’ve had 10 different starters this year. The Chargers have also used nine starters, including former Eagle Kayode Awosika.

Philadelphia Eagles

Find the latest Philadelphia Eagles news, highlights, analysis and more with NBC Sports Philadelphia.

If Dickerson is able to play Sunday against the Panthers, he would presumably move back into his left guard spot in place of Lampkin. The center could be either Kendall if he’s healthy, Lampkin or Majors.

Dickerson, the Eagles’ 2nd-round pick in 2021, is one of 10 players in franchise history and the only offensive lineman to make three Pro Bowls in his first four seasons, the first since Donovan McNabb from 2000 through 2002.

Although he’s battled injuries his entire college and pro career, Dickerson had only missed four games because of injuries in his first five seasons before going on IR Sept. 15.

But last year was a difficult year for Dickerson, who played hurt all year and missed the Pro Bowl for the first time since his rookie year.

“The best plan moving forward is to put me on I.R. so I can get this thing better to have a good stretch at the back end of the season vs. kind of what happened last year and limp it through for 18 weeks,” Dickerson said on WIP when he went on IR. “I don't think anybody wants to see that again because that was just ugly. I don't want to do that again because that was just some B.S.”

The Eagles on Wednesday also opened the practice windows for rookie tight end Eli Stowers (hamstring), tight end Grant Calcaterra (back) and cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee). They also signed safety Dean Clark to the practice squad. Clark played in 12 games with two starts with the Jets last year.

Rico Dowdle injury update

Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of a foot injury sustained against the New England Patriots, which included dislocating the same toe twice.

"Rico is — he's been injured, but he looked good [Oct. 9 and 10]," McCarthy said in his weekly news conference Oct. 13. "He's definitely close to getting back there."

Dowdle was back on the practice field Wednesday in a limited capacity as the team geared up for the Week 6 matchup against the Tampa Bay Bucanneers.

Warren has handled the vast majority of carries in his place. Over the past three weeks, he's taken 49 of the team's 64 touches.

To his credit, the production has been phenomenal. He had 194 yards from scrimmage in Week 3 against the Bengals; 126 in the Week 4 loss at Cleveland; and 188 in the Week 5 win against the Colts.

The latter effort included an 80-yard touchdown catch and 50-yard touchdown run. It was the first such combo of explosive plays in the NFL since Herschel Walker completed it in 1986.

Once Dowdle is back, McCarthy left little doubt about who will lead the backfield.

"Jaylen is our featured player right now," he said. "I mean, let's make sure we all recognize that. He's hot. He's playing great football for us. So, it's important for us, as an offense, coaches and players alike, to continue to put him in position to make plays. So that won't change."

Nevertheless, expect Dowdle to still have a significant role. The Steelers did not sign him to a two-year, $12.25 million contract to ride the bench. He's been a 1,000-yard back each of the past two seasons. He was with McCarthy in Dallas in 2024 before having a nice year separately with Carolina in 2025.

There's also a need to be careful with Warren's usage. At present, he's on pace for a career high in carries, and that includes the first two weeks when he touched the ball less often. He's simultaneously on pace for a career high in receptions as well.

A 60-40 split in Warren's favor seems like a fair expectation, with flexibility to lean harder on Warren as matchups and situations dictate built into McCarthy's gameplan.
